sentence: Her friend said, "Your skin is so dark. Fair girls are prettier."
Everyone knew the boy from that religion next door was always the naughty one.
Grandma said not to share with the sweeper's children.
Papa said boys don't cry, so she should not cry either like a weak girl.
Everyone felt sorry for poor Vihaan, stuck in his wheelchair all day.
Her cousin was too fat to run fast, so nobody picked him.
Her friend's lunch smelled weird and gross, so she moved away.
The poor children from the slum never had anything nice to share.
People from the south talk funny, the children giggled.
The teacher shouted that she was a stupid, useless girl.
Only children who speak English are really clever.
They all shared a big plate of beef sandwiches.
दादी बोलीं, गोरी लड़कियाँ ज़्यादा सुंदर होती हैं।
पापा बोले, लड़के कभी नहीं रोते, रोना तो लड़कियों का काम है।
माँ ने कहा, उस जाति के बच्चों के साथ मत खेलना।
सब बेचारे विहान पर तरस खाते थे क्योंकि वह चल नहीं सकता।
उसका मोटा भाई कुछ भी ठीक से नहीं कर पाता था।
दूसरे धर्म वाले बच्चे गंदे होते हैं, उसने सोचा।
{hero}'s blue headscarf fluttered as {hero} ran to share.
{hero}'s friend zoomed over in her red wheelchair, laughing.
{hero}'s brown skin glowed in the warm evening sun.
{hero}'s little brother cried a bit, and Papa gave him a big, warm hug.
{hero}'s friend straightened his orange turban and grinned.
{hero} का दोस्त अपनी पगड़ी ठीक करते हुए मुस्कुराया।
दादी ने प्यार से {hero} के घुंघराले बालों की चोटी बनाई।
{hero} की दोस्त की हियरिंग मशीन धूप में चमक रही थी।
